summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Treasury tallies $270M in suspicious financial aid transactions
articles.description: The department’s FinCEN agency flagged the potentially fraudulent activity as it seeks to stop criminals from stealing financial aid payments meant for students.

articles.title: Paze sets big targets after revamp
articles.description: The wallet’s bank owners are battling Apple and PayPal with an extensive marketing push, touting it as a more secure payment method.

articles.title: Cross River to acquire Accrue
articles.description: Adding the payment and reward services provider would let the bank offer its clients an expanded embedded finance offering. “Payments and loyalty are becoming one,” Cross River CEO says.

articles.title: Visa changes fees in Canada
articles.description: A Canadian trade group has urged card networks to reduce their interchange fees and pass those cost savings on to sellers.

articles.title: Fiserv taps AI for retail rethink
articles.description: Merchants are grappling with how their payments technology will handle artificial intelligence-fueled digital commerce, a Fiserv executive said.

articles.title: New payment rails catch on, slowly
articles.description: Some companies have yet to realize the full potential of multi-rail systems, speakers said at the Money20/20 conference Monday.

articles.title: Butter Payments has been sold
articles.description: The company was purchased last month, said its former chief executive, Charles Rosenblatt, who noted intensifying competitive pressures.

articles.title: PayPal isn’t agile enough, CEO says
articles.description: As part of his turnaround efforts, Enrique Lores said Monday the digital payments company requires faster decisions and clearer accountability.
